lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Kitchen Skills and Flexible Meal Planning
lessonRef.title: Application or project: measurement and timing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic measurement and timing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult present for any heat or knife steps, the learner selects one simple real recipe with at least three measured ingredients and two timed stages, gathers the correct measuring tools, and prepares the recipe following the measurements and timing exactly as written.
safetyNotes: Any step involving the stove, oven, or a sharp knife is done by or directly alongside the adult; the learner does not use these unsupervised.
Use a timer for every timed stage rather than guessing, and check food temperature or doneness the way your adult shows you.
Stop and ask for help immediately for any burn, cut, spill of hot liquid, or unfamiliar hazard.

simulationAlternative.description: If no kitchen access or ingredients are available, the learner instead reads a real recipe and, for three of its measured ingredients, converts each measurement to a different unit (for example 2 tablespoons to teaspoons) and explains what would happen to the finished dish if that ingredient's amount were doubled by mistake.

materials: adult-or-local: one simple real recipe with at least three measured ingredients and two timed stages

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one real example from this attempt where being off by a small amount, in either measurement or time, would have changed the result, and why.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Measurement accuracy: Ingredients are measured with the correct tool and leveled correctly for most steps. | Timing discipline: A timer is used for each timed stage. | Result analysis: A specific measurement or timing step is correctly identified as the likely cause of any mismatch. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner deliberately double one measurement (in a safe, edible test batch) and compare the result to the correctly measured version, describing the specific difference it caused.

resources.title: measurement and timing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult present for any heat or knife steps, the learner selects one simple real recipe with at least three measured ingredients and two timed stages, gathers the correct measuring tools, and prepares the recipe following the measurements and timing exactly as written.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact measurement and timing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before cooking, read the whole recipe once and list its measured ingredients and timed stages.
Model move 3: With your adult present for any heat or knife steps, measure and add each ingredient exactly as written, and time each stage with a timer rather than a guess.

Model check: Measurement accuracy: Ingredients are measured with the correct tool and leveled correctly for most steps. | Timing discipline: A timer is used for each timed stage. | Result analysis: A specific measurement or timing step is correctly identified as the likely cause of any mismatch.

resources.title: measurement and timing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for measurement and timing.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: measurement and timing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult present for any heat or knife steps, the learner selects one simple real recipe with at least three measured ingredients and two timed stages, gathers the correct measuring tools, and prepares the recipe following the measurements and timing exactly as written.
Coach direction: Before cooking, read the whole recipe once and list its measured ingredients and timed stages.
Learner prompt: List each measured ingredient with its exact amount, and each timed stage with its exact time.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: measurement and timing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult present for any heat or knife steps, measure and add each ingredient exactly as written, and time each stage with a timer rather than a guess.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I measured each ingredient using the correct tool (cup versus spoon) and leveled it rather than guessing a heaping amount.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I set a timer for each timed stage instead of estimating by eye.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I checked doneness the way my adult modeled before ending each timed stage.

Equal-access rule: If no kitchen access or ingredients are available, the learner instead reads a real recipe and, for three of its measured ingredients, converts each measurement to a different unit (for example 2 tablespoons to teaspoons) and explains what would happen to the finished dish if that ingredient's amount were doubled by mistake.

resources.title: measurement and timing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one real example from this attempt where being off by a small amount, in either measurement or time, would have changed the result, and why.

Success checks: Measurement accuracy: Ingredients are measured with the correct tool and leveled correctly for most steps. | Timing discipline: A timer is used for each timed stage. | Result analysis: A specific measurement or timing step is correctly identified as the likely cause of any mismatch.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: measurement and timing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional measurement and timing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Measurement accuracy: Ingredients are measured with the correct tool and leveled correctly for most steps. | Timing discipline: A timer is used for each timed stage. | Result analysis: A specific measurement or timing step is correctly identified as the likely cause of any mismatch..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u03-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Measurement accuracy: Ingredients are measured with the correct tool and leveled correctly for most steps. | Timing discipline: A timer is used for each timed stage. | Result analysis: A specific measurement or timing step is correctly identified as the likely cause of any mismatch.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
